trap-superlative.evidence: 'exactly' in 'b^2(q^{-1}) = b^2(q) exactly' is earned - I verified it symbolically: b^2 = (q^4+q^2+1)/(q^2+1)^2, and substituting q -> 1/q multiplies numerator and denominator by the same q^{-4}, so the equality is exact, not leading-order. The Taylor claims also check: hbar_q = t/(1+t) = t - t^2 + O(t^3), hbar_q^2 = t^2 - 2t^3 + O(t^4), hbar_q^4 = t^4 - 4t^5 + O(t^6), so the odd-in-t content does first appear at t^5 as stated.
